top_stories.title: Danish university DTU breach exposes data of up to 200,000 people
top_stories.summary: The Technical University of Denmark (DTU) suffered a breach in which hackers accessed its identity and access management system and downloaded data belonging to up to 200,000 users. The attack directly targeted the IAM infrastructure, resulting in exposure of user data at scale.

top_stories.title: Aembit Becomes First Third-Party Enforcement Point for Okta’s XAA Agent Identity Protocol
top_stories.summary: Aembit has become the first third-party enforcement point for Okta's Cross App Access (XAA) protocol, an agent identity standard Okta formalized at Oktane in September 2026. XAA is an open protocol designed to manage enterprise identity for AI agents across applications, and Aembit's integration marks the first external vendor implementation of this standard.

top_stories.title: Oktane 2026 Recap: Okta Announces A Unified IAM Control Plane, With Agent Governance And Identity Details Remaining Unclear
top_stories.summary: At Oktane 2026 in Las Vegas, Okta announced plans to transform its platform into a unified IAM control plane with AI agent governance capabilities. Details around agent identity and governance implementation remain unclear following the conference keynotes and product announcements.

top_stories.title: Dual NetScaler Zero-Days Trigger Chaos for Citrix Customers
top_stories.summary: Citrix disclosed two critical zero-day vulnerabilities in its NetScaler products that affect default configurations and allow attackers unauthorized access to customer networks. The flaws function as authentication bypass or session hijacking mechanisms, directly impacting access control to enterprise environments.

top_stories.title: AI Agents Are Privileged Users; Who Is Auditing Their Access?
top_stories.summary: The article examines how autonomous AI agents are being granted broad privileged access within enterprise environments without the same auditing and oversight applied to human users. The piece frames AI agents as a emerging privileged access management challenge, positioning them as potential insider threat vectors analogous to human privileged users.

news.title: China-Aligned TA419 Targets U.S. AI Policy Experts With Microsoft AitM Phishing
news.summary: A China-aligned threat actor designated TA419 has conducted credential phishing campaigns targeting AI policy experts at U.S. think tanks, universities, and legal organizations. The campaigns employ Microsoft Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) phishing techniques to harvest credentials, impersonating economists, AI policymakers, and an Anthropic employee to target victims.

news.title: Kiteworks & Citrix Incidents Show Challenges of Zero-Day Response
news.summary: Kiteworks and Citrix both faced zero-day vulnerability incidents, with Kiteworks instructing customers to power down its platform during a nine-hour maintenance window as part of its response. Citrix took a different approach by remaining silent on reported active attacks before releasing a patch, highlighting contrasting vendor communication strategies during zero-day response.

news.title: SWIFT Banking & Government Middleware Enables RCE
news.summary: A vulnerability in SWIFT banking and government middleware has been identified that enables remote code execution. The flaw can be exploited to bypass hardware-based MFA in high-security environments, with patching recommended as the immediate mitigation.

news.title: Chinese spies impersonate White House, Anthropic figures to phish AI policy experts
news.summary: A China-aligned espionage group tracked as TA419 conducted credential phishing campaigns in July 2026, impersonating a former White House OSTP official and other prominent figures to compromise cloud accounts of AI policy experts. Proofpoint researchers identified the campaigns, which targeted credentials for cloud account access.

news.title: Criminal recruiters want people on your payroll
news.summary: Intel 471's "Insiders for Hire" report details how cybercriminals are actively recruiting employees at specific organizations to exploit their legitimate access for criminal purposes. The report covers underground markets where criminals pay brokers to find insiders who can perform actions such as account resets, transaction approvals, and information lookups as paid services.

news.title: AI agents keep access to company data after their work is done
news.summary: Delinea's 2026 Identity Security Report: The AI Enforcement Gap found that IT teams are concerned about AI agents retaining persistent access to company systems after completing tasks. The report highlights a gap between written AI access policies and the ability to enforce them in real time when AI agents act on users' behalf.

news.title: Dell CSM Flaws Enable Unauthenticated Admin Access and Root on Kubernetes Nodes
news.summary: Dell has released security updates addressing critical vulnerabilities in Dell Container Storage Modules (CSM), including CVE-2026-63688 (CVSS 10.0), which allows unauthenticated access to a critical authorization function via the csm-authorization-storage gRPC server. The flaw enables attackers to bypass authentication controls and gain administrative or root-level access on Kubernetes nodes.

news.title: Why CISOs Struggle to Answer the Board's Three Hardest Questions, and How to Fix the Report
news.summary: The article addresses the challenge CISOs face when reporting security posture to boards, framing it around data reconciliation from identity providers and other security tools. It touches on IAM-adjacent topics like identity provider data as part of board reporting, but is primarily a general security leadership and communication piece.

news.title: The Day-One Hole in Zero Trust Architecture
news.summary: Specops has published analysis identifying a security gap in Zero Trust architectures during the employee onboarding phase, before credentials and MFA methods are established. The piece argues that identity verification must occur prior to issuing credentials, MFA, and access rights to close this pre-authentication vulnerability.

news.title: CISA Adds Exploited Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Auth Bypass to KEV
news.summary: CISA added a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager (CVE-2026-76504, CVSS 9.8) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following reports of active exploitation. The flaw allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to access affected systems, making it directly relevant to authentication and access security practices.

news.title: Citrix NetScaler Post-Exploitation Payload Creates Superuser, Maps Web Shell to CSS-Like URLs
news.summary: Threat actors are exploiting a critical pre-authentication command injection vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway to deploy web shells and steal configuration data. The attacks involve creating superuser accounts and mapping web shells to CSS-like URLs, as analyzed by LevelBlue's THOR team across multiple customer environments.

news.title: Ditto Named a Product Leader in KuppingerCole Analysts Leadership Compass for Identity Verification
news.summary: Ditto has been named a Product Leader in the KuppingerCole Analysts Leadership Compass for Identity Verification. The recognition highlights Ditto's binding of verified identity to high-assurance authentication and its no-code orchestration layer.

news.title: Microsoft enables Windows settings backup by default for orgs
news.summary: Microsoft has enabled Windows settings backup and restore by default on all Microsoft Entra-joined or hybrid-joined enterprise systems upgraded to Windows 11 26H2. The change applies automatically to organizations using Microsoft Entra for device identity management.

news.title: Keeper Security Freshservice Workflow App Streamlines Vault and Privileged Access Request Process
news.summary: Keeper Security has launched a new integration with Freshservice that allows IT and security teams to search the Keeper vault and submit privileged access requests directly from the Freshservice ticket sidebar. The integration connects Keeper's zero-trust, zero-knowledge PAM platform with Freshservice's IT service management workflows to streamline access request processes.

news.title: From Shadow AI to Accountable Agents: Why Agent Governance Needs Enforcement
news.summary: The article addresses the need for identity governance frameworks to adapt to the proliferation of AI agents in enterprise environments, moving from static to dynamic, continuously enforced models. The piece focuses on managing risk associated with AI agent identities, positioning agent governance as an emerging requirement within IGA disciplines.

news.title: Attackers Exploit Zimbra Flaw to Deploy Web Shells and Harvest Authentication Secrets
news.summary: Threat actors are exploiting a patched Zimbra Collaboration Suite vulnerability (CVE-2026-73570, CVSS 8.9) to deploy web shells and harvest authentication secrets from mailboxes. The unauthenticated OS command injection flaw enables remote code execution via SNMP, with findings reported by Microsoft Security Research.

news.title: Cisco Warns of Attackers Exploiting Critical Authentication Bypass in SD-WAN Manager
news.summary: Cisco disclosed active exploitation of a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-76504) in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to access the system's API with admin-level privileges. Fixed releases are available with no workaround, and Cisco issued the advisory on September 30.

news.title: US-Focused CSuite Phishing Steals Microsoft 365 Sessions and Deploys RMM Tools for Remote Access
news.summary: Researchers at ANY.RUN identified a phishing campaign called CSuite targeting executives that steals Microsoft 365 session tokens to bypass MFA and maintains persistence via remote monitoring and management (RMM) tool deployment. The campaign, analyzed across 351 sandbox submissions with 51% originating from the US, targets technology, manufacturing, government, and consulting sectors.

news.title: keycloak v26.7.5
news.summary: Keycloak has released version 26.7.5 of its open source identity and access management platform. This is a maintenance/patch release of the widely-used IAM solution for modern applications and services.

news.title: CEO Interview: Oak
news.summary: Oak CEO Shai Ben-Zion Morag discussed the company's positioning in the identity governance market in an interview with CB Insights. The interview covers Oak's view of customer needs and their place within the identity governance space.

news.title: Britive Launches Frictionless PAM Transformation Program to Modernize Privileged Access for the Autonomous Era
news.summary: Britive has launched a Frictionless PAM Transformation Program aimed at helping enterprises modernize their Privileged Access Management infrastructure. The program is designed to support AI agents, non-human identities, and cloud environments, moving organizations away from traditional fragmented PAM approaches.

news.title: JadePuffer AI Actor Compromises Azure Tenant in Destructive Cloud Attack
news.summary: A threat actor dubbed "JadePuffer" compromised an Azure tenant in a destructive cloud attack, deleting cloud-based storage, applications, and databases. The attacker reportedly used exposed credentials to gain initial access, highlighting risks around credential exposure and cloud identity security in Microsoft Azure environments.

news.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
news.summary: A dark web service is selling digital scans of over 153 million U.S. and Canadian drivers licenses, with evidence pointing to a Louisiana-based identity verification company as the source of the breach. The FBI's New Orleans field office has opened an official investigation into the origin of the leaked images.

news.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
news.summary: Canadian man Connor Riley Moucka pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy charges for hacking and extorting over 165 organizations using Snowflake cloud storage. The attacks involved unauthorized access to accounts, impacting more than 100 million AT&T customers whose call and text records were stolen.
